pr_body:
Partially fixes #20847

As we can't come up with a perfect solution the goal of this PR is just to make the situation much better.
* The first solution is to resolve rules as infrequently as possible with the introduction of `IBeforeUpdate*` interfaces.
* Second solution is to delay revolving in hopes that other update rules will fix the causes for crash

As a side effect this should make the update rules run faster as we resolve way way less yaml
pr_comments: Introduction of `IBeforeUpdate*` is as much of a fix as reordering. Updated the PR's description to an include an explanation

issue_context.title: Utility should not crash before update rules are ran
issue_context.body:
Currently we crash on yaml errors before update rules even have a chance to run. From 129db98 we resolve yaml before running update rules

This issue was found when the update rule refused to work with the crash `There are no elements with key SpawnMPUnits to remove`. 

This is unacceptable, Instead it should have first ran the `RenameMPTraits` which would have fixed the error.
comments: You could simply merge those two rules.

That wouldn't work at all. The issue here is that we resolve yaml before running rules. Merging rules doesn't adressed that, if anything, it would make the situation worse as we wouldn't have the option to run rules that don't need resolving first.

Currently we resolve before every rule, even those which don't need it
I mean merge the two conflicting/depending update rules.
If 2 large rules have nothing to do with each other and only depend due to a single variable then it doesn't feel correct
I don't see how merging rules would help, but I also think it is a bad idea - we try to have rules be as "immutable" as possible once merged to avoid issues for downstream mods that follow bleed.

review_comments: Add comments here and below explaining that these resolve rules so must be run last?
Can't we automatically sort these while running the utility?
I dunno if we want to. Some rules will give different results depending on when they are executed
It doesn't make sense to me to run these rules before the other rules that update the yaml to not crash.
Added, though I'm not sure if this is how they should look like though.

> I dunno if we want to. Some rules will give different results depending on when they are executed

Add a `int` weight to each rule? Or a stage/pass at which it should run? I.e. 'pre compile'. Perhaps distinguish between rules that modify the tree structure and those that only adjust matches. 

Or have each rule maintani a string/class-name list of rules that should run prior.
Automatic sorting would be terrible, IMO. Update rules are supposed to run in a certain order. Otherwise, they may malfunction and the update path is the place where we define the order.
#20847 sounds like you want dependency management like we do with `Requires` for traits?
Keep in mind that we should also be able to run individual rules. I have no idea how that would look.
When we have a set manually defined order of operations I really doubt that `Requires` is the correct solution
